business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vessel Hull and Cargo Damage Marine Claims Inspection Survey

Swiss-Chinese Free Trade Agreement and Joint Declaration (in force since 1 July 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on the Combating of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Anti-Money Laundering Act, AMLA/GwG), SR 951.0; Swiss Criminal Code SR 311.0, Arts. 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations SR 220, including beneficial-owner transparency provisions introduced by the 2023 corporate transparency reform; Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register SR 221.411; FINMA Circular 2016/7 on Money Laundering; Swiss Financial Services Act (FinSA) and Swiss Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FMIA) as applicable; Federal Ordinance on the Restriction of Cash Payments SR 951.71.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss or foreign notary public, Swiss embassy/consulate, or competent civil authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for signatory states; Consular Legalization for other jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract from the Criminal Record Register (Strafregisterauszug) for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Federal Office of Justice or competent cantonal criminal records authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by Swiss Federal Office of Justice or competent cantonal authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Debt Collection Register Extract (Betreibungsregisterauszug) for each Swiss-resident director and UBO, where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by cantonal authority or notarial certification for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent commercial register extract of any foreign corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required by the document's origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions database, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU and OFAC lists, and the Swiss MROS guidance for Politically Exposed Persons. Enhanced due diligence applies for PEPs under AMLA Art. 2(a). All UBOs and natural persons with management control must be identified and verified; at the 25% threshold and above, verification of identity is compulsory. For marine insurance surveying (low-risk commercial activity), standard customer due diligence is required, including KYC file, beneficial owner identification, PEP/sanctions screening, and record retention for at least 10 years under AMLA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex) of the Swiss Commercial Register, accessible at https://www.zefix.ch; filings are made through the cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt) and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOGC).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Swiss commercial register operates in the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian and Romansh). The legal-form suffix must be expressed in the corresponding official language of the registered office: 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German), 'Société anonyme' or 'SA' (French), 'Società anonima' or 'SA' (Italian). Names must be written in Latin script; words in other scripts require transliteration into one of the official Swiss languages. The name must be truthful, non-misleading, distinct from existing registered names, and must not infringe third-party trademark or names rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name clearance may be obtained from the cantonal commercial register office. Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 30 days of the rejection notification, stating the legal grounds and proposed corrective amendments. Where permitted, a single extension of the name reservation may be requested by written application before expiry. If the name is accepted, incorporation filings must be completed with the same cantonal registry before the reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure postal box without physical presence is not sufficient for a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The registered office must be located at a physical address in Switzerland and be accessible to the commercial register. For a marine insurance surveying company classified as low-risk standard activity, a service-provider virtual office with physical coordination and a local Swiss representative may be accepted, provided the company maintains a genuine administrative presence, a Swiss-resident director (or a director with Swiss residence under the Code of Obligations), and commercial substance proportionate to the claimed activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 5-8% annual risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the commercial register or tax authorities for this low-risk marine surveying company. The likelihood increases to approximately 10-15% if the company employs staff, claims VAT deductions, or engages in regulated financial insurance intermediation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register / external registered agent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220, Obligationenrecht), Arts. 620-643 (formation and registration) and Arts. 698-731 (corporate governance), read with the Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411), Arts. 7-28.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Handelsregisteramt); public notice via the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister), accompanied by notarized Articles of Association, bank blocker-account confirmation, and declarations of the incorporators.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 under Art. 621 OR; at least 20% of the nominal value of each share, and in all cases at least CHF 50,000, must be fully paid up before registration; the paid-up amount must be credited to a Swiss bank escrow (blocker) account in the name of the company in formation, with release permitted only upon presentation of the certified Commercial Register entry confirming registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription and payment of CHF 100,000 nominal share capital, of which CHF 50,000 is deposited with a licensed Swiss bank under a blocker account release to the Company upon Commercial Register entry, is hereby confirmed, and that the Articles of Association, registered office at Zug, Switzerland, and corporate purpose of marine cargo and vessel inspection surveying, loss adjusting, and technical consulting are approved; RESOLVED that the Chair of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer and the Company Secretary be appointed with binding signature authority, and that such officers be authorized to execute the registration and to open bank accounts for the Company upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize Articles of Association and Incorporation Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss civil-law notary competent for the Canton of Zug on behalf of the company in formation (Aktiengesellschaft i.G.).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association in accordance with Art. 626 OR, including the corporate name, seat, purpose (marine-cargo and vessel hull insurance inspection, loss surveying and technical consulting), share capital of CHF 100,000, share par value, number of directors, and publication organ. All incorporators must execute the deed personally or by certified proxy before the notary; retain the notarial certificate as the controlling instrument for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Identity documents of incorporators
Proof of residential address for each incorporator
Authorization and notarization engagement letter
Founders' declaration on the amount paid up
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the purpose or capital clauses, prepare a supplementary protocol and obtain re-execution without losing the underlying file; defective founders' declarations are cured by a supplemental declaration signed by all incorporators and re-notarized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocker Escrow Bank Account and Deposit Paid-up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank subject to Anti-Money Laundering Act obligations (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or comparable licensed institution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the account in the formation name of the Company and deposit the required minimum of CHF 50,000. Instruct the bank to issue a blocker-account confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) stating the credited amount, the blocking condition, and release to the Company only upon submission of the certified Commercial Register entry. The bank must complete its KYC and source-of-funds verification of all beneficial owners before issuing the confirmation.
required_dossiers: Notarized formation deed
Passport or identity card of each beneficial owner
AML/KYC questionnaire with source-of-funds proof
Beneficial-owner declaration under Swiss AML rules
Bank signature card for the formation-name account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If onboarding is refused, supplement the beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds disclosure and resubmit; if a second bank declines, transfer the instruction to another licensed bank using the same blocker-account deed, without modifying the notarized Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Commercial Register Application with the Cantonal Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), e-filing via the official cantonal portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Entry in the Commercial Register through the e-filing portal, attaching the notarized Articles of Association, blocker-account certificate, consent of directors, and declaration of authorized signatories. Identify at least one director or authorized signatory resident in Switzerland as required by Art. 718 OR. Pay the invoiced registration fee after the Registrar issues the demand.
required_dossiers: Completed Anmeldung form
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank blocker-account confirmation
Written consents of directors and authorized signatories
Proof of Swiss residency for the qualifying director
Notarized specimen signatures of authorized officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficiency notices are issued by the Registrar with a 10-day cure period; file a supplementary written declaration (Ergänzungserklärung) through the same portal, attaching the corrected documents and preserving the original filing priority; appeal a wrongful refusal to the Federal Commercial Register Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certified Registration Excerpt and SHAB Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug and the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the entry is finalized, request the official Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) containing the assigned UID number and verify its exact correspondence with the notarized deed. The Registrar forwards the incorporation entry to the SHAB for publication; preserve a certified copy for banking, tax, and license applications.
required_dossiers: Dossier reference number of the finalized registration
Proof of payment of the registration fee
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the excerpt contains material errors, file a written rectification request with the Registrar attaching the notarial deed; erroneous SHAB entries may be corrected by a supplementary public announcement without re-opening the full incorporation procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for the UID and Swiss VAT with the Federal Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Business Identification Number service and VAT registration desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the UID number via the ESTV online application using the Commercial Register excerpt. If the Company expects Swiss taxable turnover above CHF 100,000 per annum, file the mandatory VAT registration under Art. 10 of the Swiss Value Added Tax Act; export-type marine survey services supplied to foreign underwriters are eligible for zero-rating subject to documentary proof, whether or not VAT registration is applied for.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register excerpt
Completed ESTV UID application
Swiss bank account details of the Company
Turnover plan and description of marine survey services
Power of attorney if a tax agent is engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned, supplement the turnover forecast and legal-address confirmation and resubmit; if the FTA requires a Swiss service address, appoint a domiciliary agent and provide the updated address and power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Resolve Audit Appointment or Opt-Out under Art. 727a OR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Shareholders' General Meeting; licensed Swiss audit firm if a full audit is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the Company exceeds the statutory thresholds of CHF 20 million balance-sheet total, CHF 40 million turnover, and 50 full-time employees for two consecutive years. If below the thresholds, adopt a formal opt-out resolution and document it in the Board minutes; if above any threshold in the reporting year, appoint a licensed audit firm as statutory auditor and file its acceptance letter with the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Board resolution or shareholders' meeting minutes
Opt-out declaration on Form according to Swiss audit guidelines
Auditor acceptance letter if a statutory audit applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company later exceeds any threshold, the opt-out is invalid and a licensed auditor must be appointed retroactively through an extraordinary shareholders' meeting; submit the corrected resolution to the Commercial Register if the audit exception was filed there.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as Employer for Old-Age Social Insurance and Occupational Accident Cover
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zuger Ausgleichskasse for AHV/ALV employer registration and the Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund (SUVA) for UVG accident cover.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company with the cantonal compensation office as an employer after the Commercial Register entry, and obtain the employer account number and payroll reference. In parallel, declare all employees, including the directors, to SUVA under the Federal Accident Insurance Act (UVG), including the marine surveyor field assignments and office-only risk classification, and request the premium statement.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
Company bank account details
List of first employees and planned remuneration
SUVA employer questionnaire with activity classification
Copy of the articles for occupational-accident risk grading
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compensation office requests corrections, file the missing payroll data within the stated grace period; insurance liability remains statutory from the first salary payment, so late filings must be cured immediately and any administrative penalty paid to avoid enforcement measures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Municipal Operating License and Insurance-Intermediary Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of the registered office in the Canton of Zug; Cantonal Trade Office (Gewerbeamt); FINMA Insurance Intermediary Register where the company acts as an insurance intermediary under Art. 43 VAG.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the municipality for the commercial operating license covering the marine surveying office, and submit the lease agreement and floor plan with the fire-safety and building-clearance certificates. If the Company will negotiate or conclude claims settlement on behalf of insurers, register the appointed natural person in the FINMA Insurance Intermediary Register by proving professional indemnity insurance, trustworthiness, and professional qualifications; a pure surveyor providing damage assessment without intermediary functions remains outside FINMA licensing.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt
Office lease contract and floor plan
Fire safety certificate from the cantonal fire police
Professional qualification certificate of the surveying principal
Professional indemnity insurance policy
FINMA registration questionnaire if intermediary activity applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the license on zoning grounds, either obtain a building-use conversion certificate or select an alternative licensed office property within the canton and update the seat and address with the Commercial Register; FINMA deficiencies are cured by completing the professional indemnity policy and filing the supplementary statement through the FINMA portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Business Licensing Office of the Canton of Zug (Gewerbeamt des Kantons Zug); Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) for environmental components; FINMA Insurance Intermediary Register for companies performing claims-related intermediary functions under Art. 43 VAG.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Operating Permit (Gewerbebewilligung) for Marine-Insurance Inspection, Loss-Adjusting and Surveying Services, together with FINMA Insurance-Intermediary Registration under Art. 43 VAG where applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN, Bundesamt für Umwelt BAFU), in coordination with the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office of Zug.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 Registration/Exemption: office-based marine survey activities are deemed to have no significant environmental impact and require only self-declaration registration; a full EIA (Category B screening) applies only if a workshop or port-adjacent operation with hull cleaning, bilge-water handling, or hazardous-waste treatment is established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater from any controlled facility must satisfy the Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201) limit of 10 mg/L hydrocarbon oxygen-index before discharge; VOC and air-emission limits under the Swiss Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) set a 20-30 mg/m3 1-hour mean for workshop processes; oily residues and used solvents must be stored in bunded containers and transferred under the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) to authorized disposal operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Cantonal Fire-Prevention Authority confirming escape routes, fire-alarm and extinguishing systems, and evacuation signage; structural-safety attestation by a certified civil engineer confirming a minimum office-floor load-bearing capacity of 3 kN/m2; occupational health and safety clearance under SECO and SUVA standards, including first-aid equipment, accident reporting under UVG Arts. 82-88, and initial workplace risk assessment under ArGV 3.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni), Main VAT Division (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer), Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; official portal www.estv.admin.ch; corporate identifier portal www.uid.ch; commercial register search www.zefix.ch. Cantonal/communal direct taxes: competent cantonal tax authority of the registered seat (e.g., Steuerverwaltung Zug) and communal tax administrations for federal, cantonal and communal profit taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporation of the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister) automatically triggers issuance of the Swiss Business Identifier (UID-CH) ex officio by the Federal Statistical Office; no separate UID application is needed. (2) For Swiss VAT, the AG must file registration with the FTA Main VAT Division within 30 days after exceeding the statutory turnover threshold (Art. 10 para 2 lit. a, Art. 66 MWSTG). The VAT number is identical to the UID-CH with the suffix '-MWST' (e.g., CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx-MWST). Registration is delivered via the FTA online e-service (Swiss VAT registration form / MWST 31) and becomes effective on the date notified. (3) For direct federal, cantonal and communal income tax, the AG files an annual tax return with the cantonal tax authority of its statutory seat; the tax domicile is the registered office (Art. 50 DBG, Art. 20 StHG). No separate federal TIN is issued; the UID-CH serves as the uniform tax identifier for federal, cantonal and VAT purposes. (4) Foreign entities with a Swiss VAT or direct tax nexus register via the FTA foreign-entity registration form (Formular 501) and obtain a UID-CH; a foreign company operating through a Swiss permanent establishment must register its Swiss branch in the Commercial Register and file branch tax returns. (5) Re-registration obligations arise upon group VAT election (Art. 13 MWSTG), transfer of seat, or reorganization.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Swiss AG is an independent legal entity resident in Switzerland and is fully subject to Swiss corporate income tax. Statutory federal profit tax rate: 8.5% (effective approx. 4.66% after deduction of federal tax as a business expense); combined cantonal/communal effective rates (e.g., in Zug) approx. 8.5%–10.5%, yielding an overall federal-plus-cantonal effective burden typically 11.5%–15% depending on canton and finance mix. Territorial scope: unlimited tax liability on worldwide income, with relief for foreign permanent establishments and real estate via applicable double tax treaties and overall income allocation. The AG is a per se corporation under US check-the-box principles (no pass-through election available). The entity has a statutory minimum capital of CHF 100,000 (50% paid up) and unrestricted non-resident ownership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election; the AG is per se taxable. Available statutory elections and mitigation mechanisms: (1) Participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income (10% minimum holding / CHF 1 million market value threshold, Art. 20 para 1bis DBG and corresponding StHG provisions); (2) VAT group taxation election under Art. 13 MWSTG, allowing commercial consolidation for VAT purposes; (3) Option to waive VAT exemption on real estate supplies under Art. 22 MWSTG; (4) Voluntary VAT registration below the threshold to claim input VAT recovery (Art. 11 MWSTG); (5) Thin-capitalization safe-harbor structuring with prescribed debt-equity ratios applicable to shareholder loans; (6) Hybrid mismatch rules under Art. 58a–58f DBG (effective since 1 January 2020) impose automatic, non-elective matching adjustments, with disclosure-based reliefs for certain hybrid instruments; no elective anti-hybrid regime exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / Imposta sul valore aggiunto) under the Bundesgesetz über die Mehrwertsteuer of 12 June 2009 (MWSTG, SR 641.20)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 (annual turnover derived from supplies located in Switzerland for entrepreneurs domiciled or resident in Switzerland; Art. 10 para 2 lit. a MWSTG). The threshold is worldwide in respect of taxable Swiss-located turnover and includes supplies taxable at 0% as well as tax-exempt supplies attributable to the Swiss activity; it excludes supplies located abroad under the place-of-supply rules (Art. 7–8 MWSTG). A resident AG that primarily bills foreign marine underwriting recipients abroad may therefore remain unregistered if only foreign-located supplies are made; non-resident entrepreneurs are liable to Swiss VAT from the first taxable supply in Switzerland with no threshold. Registration must be filed within 30 days after the threshold is exceeded (Art. 66 MWSTG). Voluntary registration is permitted for input VAT deduction (Art. 11 MWSTG).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous API transmission or digital stamping regime applies to Swiss VAT; Switzerland operates on self-assessment and documentary audit. Mandatory invoice content under Art. 26 MWSTG: seller name/address/registration number or foreign ID, buyer name/address, date, nature of the supply, consideration, and separate statement of the VAT rate and amount. Domestic QR-billing (Swiss QR Code) and eBill are established norms; structured e-invoicing (B2G) becomes mandatory for invoices to the federal administration effective 1 January 2026. Marine surveyors should maintain Peppol BIS 3.0/electronic invoicing capability for EU recipients that impose e-invoicing. Statutory record-retention obligation: 10 years (Art. 958f CO; Art. 83 MWSTG).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Marine hull and cargo damage survey services of a Swiss AG qualify for Swiss export treatment at 0% where the services are located in Switzerland under the statutory place-of-supply rules (Art. 7–8 MWSTG) but are supplied for a foreign recipient, notably a foreign insurer, reinsurer, P&I club or shipowner. Under Art. 23 para 2 MWSTG, export zero-rating applies to services that are performed from Switzerland for the benefit of an entrepreneur situated abroad, provided the benefit is realized abroad and the recipient is proven foreign. In the conventional B2B case where the foreign underwriter is the recipient and the service is deemed supplied at the recipient's foreign seat, the supply falls entirely outside Swiss VAT (no Swiss VAT is charged and no zero-rating has to be claimed). If the surveying activity is performed on Swiss territory (e.g., Rhine port cargo inspection) and the service is nonetheless located in Switzerland for the foreign recipient, the 0% export rate can be claimed upon substantiation. Exportation of physical goods linked to survey work (test samples, equipment) follows Art. 23 para 1 MWSTG and requires a sworn Swiss customs export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung / Déclaration d'exportation) with movement reference number from Swiss Customs, where any goods are exported in connection with the survey assignment
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill, or Air Waybill/CMR road consignment note covering international movement of survey-related goods
Commercial invoice with express 0% export/foreign-supply reference, currency of account and service description of vessel hull/cargo claims inspection
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 credit advice or bank account statement documenting receipt of the survey fee from the foreign underwriter abroad
Signed survey engagement order or service contract evidencing the foreign recipient's legal address, foreign VAT/identification number and the marine insurance claims context
Survey report and navigation/damage documentation proving the executed marine hull/cargo damage inspection (ISIC 5222 scope) at the specified location
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT law contains no express statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; however, the 180-day window is applied here as the documentary settlement benchmark for zero-rating evidence (inward remittance certificate) to withstand FTA audit. Retrospective VAT assessments and input VAT clawbacks follow a 5-year limitation period in standard cases (Art. 72 para 3 MWSTG) and a 10-year period for tax evasion (Art. 71 para 3 MWSTG); default interest runs at the statutory overdue rate (currently 4.75% p.a.). Intentional VAT evasion attracts an administrative fine of up to four times the evaded tax (Art. 97 para 2 MWSTG); negligence is punishable under Art. 97 para 3 MWSTG, and jeopardizing tax revenue under Art. 96 MWSTG carries fixed regulatory fines. Fraus legis or abusive use of certificates further triggers restitution of input VAT, disqualification of the 0% rate, and re-assessment at 8.1% (or applicable reduced rates) on the full survey fee. In aggravated cases involving forged customs declarations or fictitious foreign recipients, criminal prosecution under the Swiss Criminal Code (Art. 146 fraud), the Federal Act on Administrative Criminal Law, and the direct tax evasion provisions (Art. 186–188 DBG by analogy) may result in custodial penalties and publication of the sanction. The marine surveyor must therefore preserve a complete, unbroken evidence chain: service contract, foreign-recipient identification, intercontinental transport/delivery proof, SWIFT/remittance advice, and underlying survey field records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full convertibility of the Swiss franc (CHF) on both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation for resident or non-resident shareholders, subject to corporate law solvency tests and withholding tax compliance. The SNB focuses on monetary policy and financial stability, not transactional approval. Marine insurance surveying fee receipts from foreign underwriters are classified as services on the current account and are freely creditable to Swiss bank accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds or convert foreign currency receipts into CHF. Marine survey service revenues earned from non-resident underwriters may be retained in foreign currency (e.g. USD, EUR) or converted freely. No mandatory conversion ratio or timeline applies. The only obligation is accurate reporting of cross-border service income in the corporate tax return and, where applicable, VAT treatment under Swiss value added tax law.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CHF and foreign currency sub-accounts)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse (now integrated into UBS; use alternative if unavailable)
Julius Bär Gruppe AG (Bank Julius Baer & Co. Ltd.)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-High for ancillary payment processing, but Low as a primary corporate bank account for a Swiss AG. Offshore e-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex cannot serve as a substitute for a Swiss licensed bank account for statutory corporate purposes (e.g. AG capital maintenance, Swiss withholding tax declarations, creditor protections). They may be used as secondary collection/payment rails for low-value underwriting wires if they hold an FCA/EMI license or EU EMI license, provided the company maintains its principal transactional relationship with a Swiss-regulated bank. Legal constraint: Swiss anti-money laundering (AMLA) requires the financial intermediary to be licensed in Switzerland or operate under a recognized foreign equivalent; many EMIs restrict business models involving insurance claims and surveying due to FinTech sector risk policies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors of a Swiss AG are generally required to appear in person before a notary for incorporation, but for bank account opening, Swiss banks typically require a physical meeting with at least one authorized signatory (director) at the bank branch. Some banks allow remote video identification for Swiss residents, but for non-resident directors, a physical visit or Swiss-based domiciliation agent with power of attorney is normally required. UBS and ZKB generally mandate an in-person interview for non-resident corporate clients. Remote opening is possible only via a Swiss-regulated digital onboarding process if all ultimate beneficial owners have a Swiss residence or via an existing banking relationship with a personally known client advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine insurance surveying is classified as an ISIC 5222 support activity; banks may flag the entity as a non-financial 'claims handling' intermediary that handles third-party funds if the AG receives claims proceeds on behalf of underwriters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) a copy of the licensed statutory business purpose from the Articles of Association limited to inspection and survey reporting; (2) a sworn declaration that the AG never takes custody, possession, or control of insurance claims funds; (3) standard surveyor appointment agreements with underwriters that identify the AG as an independent technical advisor only; (4) sample survey reports; (5) AML/KYC analysis confirming the company is not a virtual asset service provider or paying agent; (6) a documented internal policy prohibiting receipt of policyholder premiums or loss payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire payments from high-risk marine insurance jurisdictions (e.g. Panama, Liberia, Marshall Islands, Cyprus) may trigger enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Build a counterparty risk register showing ultimate beneficial ownership of underwriting clients, a published sanctions screening policy, and a limitation of business partners to regulated insurance companies that are themselves subject to OECD/G20 FATF supervision; provide signed onboarding questionnaires and contractual clauses mandating source-of-funds documentation for any client from a high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USE of Wise or other EMIs for receiving underwriter wires may be viewed as a fragmentation or money laundering structuring indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a treasury policy document stating that the primary account is held at a Swiss-regulated bank and that EMIs are used only for minor/disbursement efficiency; reconcile all EMI inflows to the underlying survey invoice; maintain full SWIFT/EPC payment histories; restrict withdrawals to named beneficiary accounts of suppliers; subscribe to an independent transaction monitoring solution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director structure with no Swiss physical office may trigger substance concerns and possible mailbox-company classification under Swiss banking CDB 20.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a real substance checklist: Swiss registered office, locally engaged part-time expert/claims reviewer under an employment contract, board meeting minutes held in Switzerland, insurance survey liability policy with a Swiss insurer, and an active VAT registration with Swiss turnover; provide lease agreements, payroll records, and professional indemnity insurance certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital for a Swiss AG must be deposited into a blocked Swiss bank account (Sperrkonto) verified by a Swiss notary and the Commercial Register. Subsequent capital increases use a dividend/contribution route: wire transfer from the shareholder's bank account to the AG's account at UBS/ZKB/BCV with purpose code 'Erhöhung des Aktienkapitals' or 'capital contribution reserve (Agio)'; provide beneficiary legal entity identifier (LEI), UID number, and notarized board resolution. For non-CHF injections, use MT103 with SWIFT field 72 clarifying 'Reserve from capital increase, no remuneration, no commercial transaction'; the bank will issue an exact confirmation for the commercial register. FX conversion of foreign-currency capital is permitted at market rate; the SNB has no approval role.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service fee disbursements to subcontractor surveyors, paying agents, and industry associations: use SEPA/CH-Interbank Clearing SIC for EUR/CHF within Switzerland/EEA; for non-EEA and USD remittances, use SWIFT MT103 with advantageous clearing through correspondent banks (UBS correspondent network or Citibank US for USD). For insured-client refunds or claim-related settlements where permitted, use Commercial Letter of Credit (documentary credit) only in exceptional pre-advance payment scenarios; standard practice for service disbursements is corporate credit transfer, not LC. ACH/EBPP rails are not used for high-value cross-border disbursements. VAT-flagged payments require distinctly annotated purpose codes such as 'Insurance surveying services, no claims handling' to avoid misinterpretation under AML rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) OTC with UBS, ZKB, or BCV under an ISDA/CSA master agreement, permitted for trade-related exposure up to 12 months tenor
FX swaps (swap/roll of spot and forward) for working capital rebalancing

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible but unnecessary for CHF as CHF is fully convertible; only warranted for exotic currencies like Nigerian Naira or Egyptian Pound if payments come from distressed marine jurisdictions
Currency swaps with a maturity above 12 months for matched purpose (e.g. foreign currency loan hedging), requiring treasury policy approval and Swiss bank credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal, cantonal and communal corporate income/profit tax return (combined assessment form for Federal Direct Tax and cantonal/communal taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered office with informational coordination by Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year AG, due by 31 March following the tax year; administrative extension normally available to 31 December of the following year. Final assessment usually issued within 12 months after the fiscal year close.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid taxes, administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 for false omission, criminal referral for intentional tax evasion, and eventual enforced collection and commercial register strike-off procedure after failed execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual or periodic Swiss VAT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV - VAT Division)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the close of the VAT settlement period (quarterly, half-yearly or annual depending on turnover). Electronic filing through ESTV portal is required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on late VAT, fixed penalty calculated on the amount of tax threatened, fine up to CHF 8,000 for gross negligence, and enforced collection which may lead to commercial register deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting adoption of annual financial statements, discharge of directors, and signed minutes filed in the Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; meeting records and minutes retained at the registered office for inspection by the Commercial Register authority or auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened and held within six months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors bear civil liability for losses; court may compel the AGM upon shareholder request; continued failure to regularize corporate governance can trigger commercial register formal notice and strike-off under Art. 731b of the Swiss Code of Obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual OASI/AHV/AVS wage declaration and employer social security contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss AHV compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse) competent for the registered office of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employer wage statement due by 31 March of the following year; contribution settlement invoice follows after verification of the reconciled wage data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge, default interest on unpaid social security contributions, fines for deliberate incorrect declarations, and enforced debt collection that may support a commercial register strike-off procedure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary independent audit applies if two of the following three thresholds are exceeded in two consecutive financial years: CHF 20,000,000 balance sheet total, CHF 40,000,000 annual turnover, and 250 average full-time employees. Below these thresholds a qualified limited audit is required unless all shareholders unanimously waive the audit, which is permitted only when the company does not exceed 10 full-time employees on annual average.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 958-963b) accounting rules; financial statements prepared in CHF and in accordance with applicable Swiss GAAP standards. IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER may be adopted voluntarily for statutory reporting if consistently applied; IFRS/FER is mandatory for listed companies and certain regulated financial entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss AG law does not require an annual UBO form to be submitted to the Commercial Register. The board must audit the shareholders' register before each ordinary AGM, record all share transfers made during the financial year, and confirm the identity of beneficial owners for registered shares when a shareholder is not the beneficial owner. For every transfer exceeding 5% of voting rights, the company must demand beneficial-owner identification. The updated shareholder and beneficial-owner record must remain available at the registered office for Commercial Register inspection and is not a public filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,800-8,000 per year for standard registered office, correspondence management and corporate secretarial maintenance in a non-premium Swiss canton; Zug or Geneva full-service provider may reach USD 10,000-12,000.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000-22,000 for a qualified limited audit of a small AG; USD 25,000-50,000 for a full ordinary statutory audit of a mid-sized AG with substantive marine surveying claims administration activity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (imposed on after-tax profit; equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit). Combined federal, cantonal and communal headline rate ranges from approximately 11.9% (Zug) to 21.0% (Geneva) depending on the canton of domicile.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays apply to ISIC 5222 marine surveying. Permanent preferential regimes: participation relief exempting the preponderance of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from participations of at least 10% or CHF 1,000,000 market value at both federal and cantonal level; canton-level patent box excluding up to 90% of IP-derived profit; notional interest deduction in introducing cantons; R&D super-deduction of 50% of qualifying R&D staff and third-party costs. A substance-rich surveying AG typically achieves an effective rate of 11.9% to 18%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal/municipal corporate tax return (Steuererklärung fuer juristische Personen / Formulaire pour personnes morales) of the canton of seat, filed electronically via the cantonal e-filing portal (e.g., InTax, TaxMe, TaxOnline, ESTHER, depending on canton). The return incorporates the cantonal, municipal and federal direct tax declarations in one filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Provisional quarterly instalments of the expected corporate tax are paid during the tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The statutory filing deadline is fixed by the canton of seat, normally within four to six months after the end of the business year. For a 31 December year-end the return is commonly due between 31 March and 30 June of the following year; extensions up to twelve months are granted on application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, legal form (AG), seat, business purpose, UID and VAT numbers, board members and authorised signatories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Swiss registered office and the Swiss resident director; list non-resident shareholders only in the supplementary participation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities, issued share capital, legal reserves and retained earnings; determines the capital tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Evidence paid-in capital from non-resident shareholders with bank statements and the share register; undue shareholder loans are reclassified as equity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Profit and loss reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before tax after adjustment for non-deductible expenses, hidden distributions and reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back excess management, licence or surveyor fees paid to non-resident affiliates unless arm's-length proof is attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of participation relief on qualifying dividend income and capital gains (10% threshold or CHF 1,000,000 participation value).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the holding register and confirmation of the participation percentage; relief is denied where the shareholding serves only portfolio purposes without substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign permanent establishment profits and foreign real-estate income exempt under double taxation agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate direct and indirect expenses to the exempt foreign stream; foreign tax assessments support the claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of cross-border intercompany services, royalties, loans and reinsurance or survey commissions; transfer pricing method and documentation index.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Local File and Master File where group turnover thresholds are met; use OECD-aligned CUP, Cost Plus or TNMM for marine survey fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a procedural administrative fine of up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG), default interest of approximately 3.5% p.a. on the overdue federal tax, and cantonal late surcharges of 0.5% per month up to 25% of the assessed tax. Persistent non-filing triggers arbitrary assessment with a reversed burden of proof.
